q-126558.name: Question 1
q-126558.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14251407/assets/7264984a1c19c247c030feae04615bb0c46205ca70475db1240db964ad6007b2.png)

Suppose that $F$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ defined over the region $D$ above. Given that 

$$
{∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r=10,\,{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r=-4,\,{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r=-2,
$$

where ${C}_{1}$ is oriented counterclockwise and ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ are oriented clockwise, calculate the value of ${∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r.$
q-126558.worked_solution:
To calculate the total circulation of a vector field over the boundary of a region containing holes, we add together the circulations over each *positively oriented* boundary.

Remember that:

- the positive direction is *counterclockwise* for the *outer* curve ${C}_{1}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{1}$ counterclockwise), and

- the positive direction is *clockwise* for the *inner* curves ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ clockwise).

The diagram below shows the positive orientations of all three curves.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14251407/assets/0de833fcc39b6295418c1558cf1187774db7b4ada1d697f2dcac8c35858563df.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =10-4-2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

q-126880.name: Question 5
q-126880.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14251407/assets/65047f9bf4f035000175fc55ee3ba6eeb4aa7ec39674a1984b95ba98a3f754f6.png)

Calculate ${∮}_{∂D}8y\,dx+13x\,dy,$ where $D$ is the region shown above.
q-126880.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Green's theorem can be extended to include regions containing holes. In such cases, we can apply Green's theorem in the same way as before.

We have that $P(x,y)=8y$ and $Q(x,y)=13x.$ So,  

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=8,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=13.
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}8y\,dx+13x\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(13-8)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}5\,\text{d}A \\  & =5\,{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & =5\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =5\cdot (\frac{6\cdot 6}{2}-{2}^{2}) \\  & =5\cdot (18-4) \\  & =70.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

Calculate ∮∂D8ydx+13xdy, where D is the region shown above.

a

Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let C be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let D be the region bounded by C. If P and Q have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing D, then Green's theorem states that ∮CPdx+Qdy=∬D(∂Q∂x−∂P∂y)dA.

Green's theorem can be extended to include regions containing holes. In such cases, we can apply Green's theorem in the same way as before.

We have that P(x,y)=8y and Q(x,y)=13x. So,

∂P∂y=8,∂Q∂x=13.

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

∮∂D8ydx+13xdy=∬D(∂Q∂x−∂P∂y)dA=∬D(13−8)dA=∬D5dA=5∬DdA=5⋅Area(D)=5⋅(6⋅62−22)=5⋅(18−4)=70.
